BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 2 1. Purpose and Scope BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. is a fictional technology services company. This handbook defines common workplace expectations and general employee practices for full-time employees, interns, and fixed-term employees unless a specific policy states otherwise. Where this handbook conflicts with a dedicated policy, the dedicated policy takes precedence. 2. Company Overview BlueOrbit provides software engineering, analytics, cloud, and business technology services to clients in India and selected international markets. Core values: integrity, customer focus, ownership, collaboration, continuous learning, and respect. Standard working hours: 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM local office time, Monday through Friday, with a one-hour

collaboration, continuous learning, and respect. Standard working hours: 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM local office time, Monday through Friday, with a one-hour lunch break. Teams may have approved schedules that differ because of client or operational requirements. 3. Attendance and Punctuality Employees are expected to be available during their approved working schedule and to record attendance through the designated HR system. • Employees should inform their manager as early as possible when they expect to be late or absent. • Repeated unapproved absence or attendance irregularities may be reviewed by the manager and HR. • Remote employees must remain reachable during core working hours defined by the applicable Work From Home Policy.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 3 4. Employee Conduct and Code of Ethics Employees must act honestly, respectfully, and professionally when dealing with colleagues, clients, vendors, and visitors. • Harassment, discrimination, intimidation, retaliation, and workplace violence are prohibited. • Employees must protect confidential company and client information. • Conflicts of interest must be disclosed to the manager or HR. • Company resources must be used primarily for legitimate business purposes. 5. Workplace Behavior Employees should maintain a professional environment, respect different viewpoints, communicate constructively, and avoid behavior that disrupts others. Employees are responsible for following the Security Policy when handling company devices, credent

ructively, and avoid behavior that disrupts others. Employees are responsible for following the Security Policy when handling company devices, credentials, data, email, and external storage. 6. Office Access and Facilities Employees may enter only offices and areas for which they have authorization. Visitors must follow reception and visitor-registration procedures. Employees must display or carry their company identification badge as required by the office. Office facilities such as meeting rooms, cafeterias, parking, and collaboration spaces should be used responsibly.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 4 7. Holidays and Leave Company holidays are published annually by HR for each office location. Leave entitlements and approval requirements are governed by the Leave Policy. Employees should not rely on this handbook for individual leave balances. 8. Probation New employees normally complete a six-month probation period unless their employment letter specifies otherwise. During probation, performance, attendance, conduct, and role fit are reviewed. Leave eligibility during probation is subject to the Leave Policy and applicable employment terms. 9. Performance Reviews Formal performance reviews are normally conducted twice each year. Managers may also provide informal feedback throughout the year. Reviews may consider delivery, qualit

reviews are normally conducted twice each year. Managers may also provide informal feedback throughout the year. Reviews may consider delivery, quality, collaboration, ownership, customer impact, learning, and adherence to company policies.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 5 10. Promotions and Career Development Promotions are based on demonstrated performance, role expectations, business requirements, skills, and sustained impact. Completion of a minimum tenure does not automatically guarantee promotion. Employees are encouraged to discuss development goals with their manager during regular one-on-ones. 11. Employee Responsibilities • Follow company policies and applicable laws. • Protect company property and confidential information. • Complete required training on time. • Report security incidents, workplace concerns, and policy violations through the appropriate channels. • Keep personal and emergency contact information up to date in the HR system. 12. HR and Support Contacts HR Helpdesk: hr@blueorb

propriate channels. • Keep personal and emergency contact information up to date in the HR system. 12. HR and Support Contacts HR Helpdesk: hr@blueorbit.example IT Helpdesk: ithelp@blueorbit.example Security Incident Hotline: security@blueorbit.example Use the internal employee portal for current contact details and service-request procedures. 13. Policy References This handbook should be read together with the Leave Policy, Travel Policy, Work From Home Policy, and Security Policy. Those documents contain more specific requirements for their respective topics.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 1 BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. LEAVE POLICY Document ID: BO-HR-002 | Version: 2.0 | Effective Date: 01-Apr-2026 Document Status: Approved Owner: Human Resources / Corporate Operations

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 2 1. Purpose and Scope This policy defines paid leave categories, eligibility, carry-forward rules, application procedures, and approval requirements for BlueOrbit employees. Leave balances are maintained in the employee HR system. This policy describes the rules; it does not provide an employee's individual balance. 2. Leave Categories and Annual Entitlement Casual Leave (CL): 12 days per calendar year. Earned Leave (EL): 18 days per calendar year for eligible employees. Sick Leave (SL): 12 days per calendar year. Leave is generally prorated for employees joining during the calendar year, subject to HR rules and employment terms. 3. Casual Leave Casual leave is intended for short personal needs, appointments, urgent family matters, or

, subject to HR rules and employment terms. 3. Casual Leave Casual leave is intended for short personal needs, appointments, urgent family matters, or other brief absences. Employees should request casual leave in advance where reasonably possible. Casual leave normally cannot be carried forward beyond the calendar year.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 3 4. Earned / Annual Leave Earned leave is intended for planned vacations and longer personal breaks. Carry-forward limit: up to 12 unused earned-leave days may be carried into the following calendar year. Any balance above the permitted carry-forward limit is normally forfeited at year-end unless HR approves an exception. 5. Sick Leave Sick leave is intended for illness or medical recovery. Employees should notify their manager as soon as practicable when illness prevents attendance. A medical certificate may be requested for extended absence or where required by HR. 6. Eligibility and Probation Employees become eligible for leave according to their employment terms and applicable statutory requirements. During probation: employees ma

robation Employees become eligible for leave according to their employment terms and applicable statutory requirements. During probation: employees may use accrued eligible leave subject to manager approval and HR rules. Leave does not automatically become available in full on the joining date.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 4 7. Carry-Forward Rules Only earned leave is eligible for standard carry-forward. Maximum carry-forward: 12 earned-leave days into the next calendar year. Casual and sick leave balances normally expire at the end of the calendar year unless applicable law or an approved exception provides otherwise. 8. Leave Application Process • Submit the leave request through the HR/leave management system. • Select the leave category and requested dates. • Provide a brief reason when the system or manager requires one. • Obtain manager approval before taking planned leave. • Update the request promptly if dates change. 9. Manager Approval and Emergency Leave Managers review leave based on team coverage, business needs, and policy eligibility. Emer

ly if dates change. 9. Manager Approval and Emergency Leave Managers review leave based on team coverage, business needs, and policy eligibility. Emergency leave may be communicated by phone or approved communication channel when advance application is not practical. The employee should regularize the leave request in the HR system afterward.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 5 10. Leave During Notice Period Leave during the notice period requires manager and HR approval and may be subject to operational requirements and applicable employment terms. 11. Questions and Escalation For policy interpretation, contact HR. For an employee's current balance, use the HR system or the employee leave-balance service rather than this document.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 1 BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. INFORMATION SECURITY POLICY Document ID: BO-SEC-001 | Version: 2.0 | Effective Date: 01-Apr-2026 Document Status: Approved Owner: Human Resources / Corporate Operations

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 2 1. Purpose and Scope This policy establishes minimum security requirements for BlueOrbit systems, devices, accounts, and company information. It applies to employees, interns, contractors, and other authorized users handling BlueOrbit or client information. 2. Password Requirements Passwords must be unique and must not be reused across personal and company services. Employees must not share passwords or store them in unapproved locations. Use the company-approved password manager where provided. Suspected credential compromise must be reported immediately. 3. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) MFA is required for supported company applications and remote access. Employees must never approve an unexpected MFA request. Unexpected prompt
(MFA) MFA is required for supported company applications and remote access. Employees must never approve an unexpected MFA request. Unexpected prompts may indicate an attempted account compromise.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 3 4. Company Laptop Usage Company laptops are intended primarily for authorized business use. Employees must lock their screens when unattended. Operating system and security updates must not be intentionally disabled or delayed. Only authorized users may use company devices. 5. Personal Devices Personal devices must not be used to access restricted or confidential systems unless explicitly approved and protected by required controls. Company data must not be copied to personal storage, personal email, or unapproved messaging applications. 6. Software Installation Employees may install only software approved by BlueOrbit or its IT team. Pirated, cracked, unlicensed, or security-risk software is prohibited. Requests for business softwar
ly software approved by BlueOrbit or its IT team. Pirated, cracked, unlicensed, or security-risk software is prohibited. Requests for business software should be submitted to IT.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 4 7. Data Classification and Confidential Information Public: information approved for public release. Internal: routine company information intended for employees. Confidential: business, employee, financial, client, or technical information that requires controlled access. Restricted: highly sensitive information requiring strict access controls. Confidential and Restricted information must be shared only with authorized recipients through approved systems. 8. Phishing and Email Security Employees should verify unexpected links, attachments, payment requests, password requests, and urgent messages. Do not enter company credentials into suspicious pages. Report suspected phishing to security@blueorbit.example or through the security r

nt messages. Do not enter company credentials into suspicious pages. Report suspected phishing to security@blueorbit.example or through the security reporting mechanism. 9. VPN and Remote Access Employees must use approved remote-access methods for systems that require VPN. VPN credentials must not be shared. Public or shared computers must not be used for company remote access.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 5 10. Lost or Stolen Device Procedure Immediate action: If a company laptop or mobile device is lost or stolen, report it to IT and Security immediately. Do not attempt to recover a stolen device yourself if doing so creates a safety risk. Security may remotely lock, disable, or wipe a managed device where technically possible. Employees should change potentially exposed credentials when instructed by Security. 11. USB and External Storage USB drives and external storage may be used only when approved and when required security controls are in place. Confidential or Restricted data must not be copied to unapproved removable media. 12. Public Wi-Fi Avoid accessing sensitive systems over open public Wi-Fi. When remote access is necessary

ot be copied to unapproved removable media. 12. Public Wi-Fi Avoid accessing sensitive systems over open public Wi-Fi. When remote access is necessary, use an approved secure connection and VPN where required. Never disable endpoint security controls to improve connectivity. 13. Incident Reporting Report suspected security incidents immediately, including phishing, malware, lost devices, accidental data exposure, unauthorized access, or credential compromise. Security contact: security@blueorbit.example IT contact: ithelp@blueorbit.example

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 1 BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. TRAVEL & EXPENSE POLICY Document ID: BO-TRV-001 | Version: 2.0 | Effective Date: 01-Apr-2026 Document Status: Approved Owner: Human Resources / Corporate Operations

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 2 1. Purpose and Scope This policy governs business travel undertaken on behalf of BlueOrbit and defines approval, booking, accommodation, meals, local transportation, and expense-claim requirements. Personal travel costs are not reimbursable unless specifically approved as a business exception. 2. Business Travel Eligibility Business travel must have a legitimate business purpose such as client meetings, project work, conferences, training, or approved company events. Employees should use cost-effective options while considering safety, business requirements, and reasonable travel time. 3. Travel Approval Travel should be approved by the employee's manager before booking. International travel additionally requires the relevant busines

3. Travel Approval Travel should be approved by the employee's manager before booking. International travel additionally requires the relevant business and HR/security approvals where applicable. Unapproved travel may not be reimbursed.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 3 4. Air and Train Travel Domestic air travel: Economy class is the standard entitlement. International air travel: Economy class is standard unless an executive-level exception is approved. Train travel: AC Chair Car or AC 2-Tier is reimbursable for eligible business travel, depending on journey duration and availability. Employees should use approved corporate booking channels when available. 5. Accommodation Domestic hotel allowance: up to ₹5,000 per night, excluding taxes. International hotel allowance: up to ₹12,000 per night equivalent, excluding taxes, unless a location-specific limit is approved. Hotel claims should include an itemized invoice or receipt. Accommodation above the standard limit requires prior approval; an except

mit is approved. Hotel claims should include an itemized invoice or receipt. Accommodation above the standard limit requires prior approval; an exception is not guaranteed simply because the employee incurred the cost. 6. Meals Domestic meal allowance: up to ₹1,200 per day for breakfast, lunch, and dinner combined when meals are not provided by the company or host. International meal allowance: up to ₹3,500 per day equivalent. Alcoholic beverages are not reimbursable. Meal receipts should be retained when required by the expense system.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 4 7. Local Transportation and Mileage Local transport: reasonable taxi, ride-hailing, public transport, or approved rental costs are reimbursable for business purposes. Personal vehicle mileage: ₹12 per kilometer for approved business travel using a personal car. Parking and tolls may be reimbursed when directly related to approved business travel and supported by receipts. 8. Expense Claims and Receipts Employees must submit travel expenses within 15 calendar days after returning from the trip. Receipts are required for hotel, air/train tickets, local transportation, and other claim categories where the expense system requests supporting evidence. Missing documentation may delay reimbursement or result in rejection. 9. Travel Advance

gories where the expense system requests supporting evidence. Missing documentation may delay reimbursement or result in rejection. 9. Travel Advance Employees may request a travel advance for approved trips when permitted by the finance process. Unused advance amounts must be settled through the expense claim process within 15 calendar days after travel.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 5 10. International Travel and Security Employees traveling internationally must comply with visa, insurance, security, and destination-specific requirements. Sensitive company information must be protected during travel. Public Wi-Fi should be used only with approved security controls and VPN where required. 11. Exceptions and Contacts Exceptions to monetary limits require documented approval from the appropriate business or finance authority before the expense is incurred whenever practical. Finance support: finance@blueorbit.example Travel support: travel@blueorbit.example

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 1 BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. WORK FROM HOME POLICY Document ID: BO-WFH-001 | Version: 2.0 | Effective Date: 01-Apr-2026 Document Status: Approved Owner: Human Resources / Corporate Operations

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 2 1. Purpose and Scope This policy defines the conditions under which eligible BlueOrbit employees may work remotely. WFH availability is subject to role suitability, team requirements, performance, security controls, and manager approval. 2. WFH Eligibility Employees in roles suitable for remote work may request WFH. Roles requiring physical presence, specialized equipment, customer-site work, or other operational coverage may have different arrangements. Eligibility does not create an automatic right to work remotely on any specific day. 3. Monthly WFH Allowance Standard allowance: up to 8 WFH days per calendar month for eligible employees. Unused WFH days do not carry forward to the next month. Managers may approve fewer WFH days wh

o 8 WFH days per calendar month for eligible employees. Unused WFH days do not carry forward to the next month. Managers may approve fewer WFH days when business or team requirements require regular office presence.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 3 4. Approval Requirements Planned WFH should be requested through the designated attendance/HR system before the workday begins. Manager approval is required unless the request qualifies as emergency WFH. Employees should ensure their calendar and team availability status accurately reflect their working location. 5. Consecutive WFH Limit Standard limit: a maximum of 3 consecutive WFH working days may be taken under a normal request. Requests exceeding 3 consecutive working days require manager and HR approval and may be treated as an exception. 6. Core Working Hours Core hours: 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM local time. Employees working remotely must remain reachable during core hours unless they are on an approved break, leave, or exception.

to 4:00 PM local time. Employees working remotely must remain reachable during core hours unless they are on an approved break, leave, or exception. Team-specific schedules may require additional availability.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 4 7. Availability and Performance Employees must attend required meetings, respond through approved communication channels, and maintain expected productivity. WFH should not be used to avoid required office attendance, client meetings, training, or team events. 8. Emergency WFH Emergency WFH may be requested for unexpected situations that make office attendance impractical. Employees should notify their manager as soon as possible and regularize the attendance record afterward. 9. Equipment Requirements Employees should use company-approved devices and accessories where provided. Home internet should be sufficiently reliable for normal work requirements. Company equipment must not be shared with unauthorized persons.

BlueOrbit Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Internal Use Only Page 5 10. Security Requirements Employees must follow the Security Policy while working remotely. • Use MFA and approved authentication methods. • Do not store confidential company data on personal devices or unapproved cloud storage. • Use the company VPN when required for sensitive systems. • Position screens to prevent unauthorized viewing in public or shared spaces. • Report lost devices or suspected security incidents immediately. 11. Exceptions and Contact Exceptions may be approved based on business need, health/safety considerations, or other documented circumstances. HR: hr@blueorbit.example Manager approval: the employee's direct manager or designated delegate
